question: Under fixed stimuli and matched resource budgets, does certified e-graph feedback improve LLM assertion/monitor correctness, effective fault detection and cost efficiency?

task.selection_priority: One bounded multi-cycle request/response controller with backpressure and explicit cancellation/reset semantics
task.policy: Select by specification clarity, relevant nontrivial guard mappings and formal tractability before new B/C outcomes. One task first; do not inherit the original stimulus-difficulty gate or claim two independent IPs. Do not construct a task to force C gains.

shared_budget_draft.note: Equal caps across arms; actual input/output tokens, retries, compile/replay/formal work and wall time remain measured separately. Final schedule and property/monitor limits must be filled before freeze; no arm-specific retries or resource extensions.

role_boundary.reference: Claude specification-only checker author plus fresh independent reviewer; no GPT oracle substitution or silent repair
role_boundary.candidate: GPT generates the evaluated passive assertions/monitors
role_boundary.infrastructure: GPT/Codex builds drivers, isolation, scoring and accounting; no candidate-defined truth

feedback_contract.shared: Frozen spec, public RTL/interface, identical fixed development observations and all raw DUT counter identities/counts; identical compile and development feedback policies
feedback_contract.C_only: Certified, task-relevant equivalent guards with widths, signedness, full activation, source mapping and clock/reset context; no sequential or spec-correctness inference
feedback_contract.raw_coverage: Fixed measurement, never a candidate-optimized endpoint; never merge source counters
feedback_contract.length_control: No placebo arm authorized by this draft. Without a separately registered token-matched placebo, interpret C versus B as a whole feedback-package effect.

release_and_scoring.fresh_final_corpus: Required; v1 final cases and saved candidates are infrastructure calibration only
release_and_scoring.snapshot_policy: Freeze source/metadata for every generated round before hidden scoring; final candidate chosen only by predeclared validity and round order. Score snapshots offline after the full release, with no hidden feedback or post-score repair.
primary: candidate validity and zero-false-alarm/unknown rate on independently validated legal controls
distinct independently confirmed observable fault recall
valid distinct detections per 1000 actual API input+output tokens
secondary: predeclared cost-to-quality endpoint if defined before calls
formal bounded results and complete proofs separately
timeouts, unknowns, invalid/missing candidates and all costs
release_and_scoring.truth: Independent spec reference determines observability and first violation; no credit for an alarm before a reference-confirmed violation. Simulation controls, activation cover, bounded checks and unbounded proof are separate evidence.
release_and_scoring.failure_policy: Retain failures and not-reached results; TIMEOUT/UNKNOWN/ERROR never PASS; all invalid attempts and costs stay in raw denominators

stop_policy: Do not launch reference/candidate calls from this draft. Complete a single-task feasibility packet, then bind all missing fields and gates in a new immutable registration/live freeze. Preserve negative preflights; no task or budget tuning against C outcomes. Stage credentials only through the existing terminal hidden-input helper when a concrete API stage is ready.
